newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London led up by HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London led up by HSBC.

text.p: The Hang Seng London Reference Index was pulled up on Thursday by strong demand for HSBC shares, dealers said.
Trade in other shares was quiet, with the Hong Kong bourse shut for the Lunar New Year, but a HK$4-1/4 gain in HSBC helped lift the index 56.29 points to 13,716.79 by 1346 GMT.
"Apparently there is a shortage of HSBC shares in London and people can't buy them in Hong Kong because the market's closed, so they've been buying the Hong Kong share here," one dealer said.
"That accounts for the majority of the gain in the index. Other banks are slightly up in sympathy, but not very much, it's really just HSBC today," he said.
The Hong Kong stock exchange remains closed on Friday. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4367
